page: Amazon Web Services c5.xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8124M processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The instance provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 8.0 GB of DDR4 memory running at 3 GHz, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per core. There is no local storage or GPU hardware bundled with this instance, and network connectivity is limited to a 1 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities but weaker multi-core and memory performance. The single-core Geekbench score of 1157.0 and stress-ng single-core CPU performance of 1493.19 fall into the average tier, supported by average single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression rates. However, multi-core benchmarks show limitations, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 2536.0 and a passmark CPU score of 4592.75, both categorized as weak. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, registering at 26.42 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 23.29 GB/sec for large block write operations, resulting in a poor Passmark memory score of 1078.56.

Given its compute-focused hardware profile, the c5.xlarge offers qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require dedicated CPU cycles but have low memory footprints. The lack of local storage and lower network bandwidth baseline make it less suitable for high-throughput database operations or large-scale data streaming. Instead, it is best suited for single-threaded or moderately threaded compute tasks, lightweight web serving, and basic batch processing where memory capacity and multi-core scaling are not the primary bottlenecks.
